extracted.intended_audience: machine learning / NLP researchers working on mathematical reasoning and language models
extracted.subtask_short: training verifiers for math word problems
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and evaluating verifier models that judge correctness of language-model solutions to grade-school math word problems (using the GSM8K dataset), and using verifier rankings at test time to select among many candidate solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: GSM8K dataset quality
rubrics_metrics.description: A dataset of 8.5K high quality linguistically diverse grade school math word problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to diagnose failures of current models; emphasizes problem quality (high quality), linguistic diversity, and grade-school difficulty level. Size (8.5K) and diversity are presented as important dataset characteristics for evaluating multi-step math reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-step mathematical reasoning ability
rubrics_metrics.description: State-of-the-art language models still struggle to robustly perform multi-step mathematical reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The primary capability being evaluated is robustness on multi-step reasoning tasks — i.e., producing correct multi-step solutions — which the paper uses GSM8K to measure. Robustness to multi-step reasoning errors is a central evaluative criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifier correctness judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Training verifiers to judge the correctness of model completions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verifiers are models trained to assess whether a candidate solution is correct. The paper proposes this as an evaluation/selection component: instead of only relying on the generator, train a separate verifier whose judgments are used to choose among candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate generation and selection by ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: At test time, generate many candidate solutions and select the one ranked highest by the verifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inference procedure combines generator diversity (many sampled/written candidate completions) with verifier ranking; success depends on both generating sufficient candidate diversity and accurate verifier ranking to pick a correct solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test performance and scaling with data (verification vs. finetuning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification significantly improves performance on GSM8K, and verification scales more effectively with increased data than a finetuning baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key evaluation metrics are absolute test performance on GSM8K and how performance scales as more data is available. The paper positions verification-based selection as outperforming/being more data-efficient than straightforward finetuning baselines.
